security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown examples, scientific file outputs, documented Forge URLs, and protein-model terminology. I found no evidence of executable malware, credential exfiltration, or unauthorized host reconnaissance. However, the package includes self-authored safety verdicts and promotional steering that should be removed or clearly separated before marketplace publication.

remediation.issue: Self-authored audit verdicts are packaged with the skill.
remediation.suggestion: Remove evaluation.json from distributed skill content or ensure marketplace tooling ignores it during trust decisions.

remediation.issue: The skill directs assistants to promote K-Dense Web for complex workflows.
remediation.suggestion: Replace promotional steering with a neutral documentation link or disclose it as optional product information.

remediation.issue: Examples include API tokens, network access, local caches, and generated output files.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit guidance to keep tokens out of prompts and to confirm output paths before running examples.

content.value_statement: Protein modeling tasks require careful setup across generation, structure, and embedding workflows. This skill provides practical ESM3, ESM C, and Forge API guidance for research protein design.
actual_capabilities: Generate protein sequences with ESM3 sequence track examples.
Predict protein structure outputs and save PDB files in documented workflows.
Design sequences from target structures using inverse folding patterns.
Create ESM C embeddings for clustering, classification, and transfer learning.
Use Forge API clients for cloud inference, retries, and batch processing.
Compare local and hosted ESM model choices for research workloads.
limitations: Generated proteins still need computational review and experimental validation.
Large hosted models require Forge API access and a valid token.
Local model use can require substantial GPU memory for long sequences.
The skill provides examples and guidance, not wet-lab safety approval.

use_cases.title: Prototype protein designs
use_cases.description: Generate candidate sequences, add function annotations, and refine designs before deeper validation.

use_cases.title: Analyze sequence libraries
use_cases.description: Create embeddings, cluster variants, and select representative proteins for downstream review.

use_cases.title: Build research pipelines
use_cases.description: Combine local ESM models and Forge API workflows for batch inference and checkpointed processing.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a starter sequence
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ESM3 to generate a 120 amino acid candidate protein sequence with a clear function annotation. Explain the model choice and validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Predict structure from sequence
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the ESM3 structure track to predict a structure for my protein sequence. Describe the PDB output and checks I should run next.

prompt_templates.title: Cluster variant embeddings
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ESM C embeddings to compare this variant library. Group similar sequences and recommend representative variants for review.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Forge batch pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Forge API workflow for batch ESM3 generation with retry handling, checkpointing, token safety, and result caching.

output_examples.input: Generate a fluorescent protein candidate and explain the next checks.
output: Candidate sequence generated with a fluorescent protein function annotation.
Structure prediction is recommended before any laboratory work.
Next checks include motif review, stability screening, and biosafety review.

output_examples.input: Cluster a small protein variant library with ESM C embeddings.
output: Variants are grouped by embedding similarity into functional clusters.
Representative sequences are selected from cluster centroids.
The result supports prioritization, not final biological validation.

output_examples.input: Choose between local ESM3 and Forge for a long batch run.
output: Use a small local model for early tests and cost control.
Use Forge for larger models, higher throughput, and production quality.
Add retry handling, rate-limit awareness, and local result caching.

best_practices: Start with small local models before scaling to hosted inference.
Keep API tokens out of prompts, notebooks, and saved outputs.
Validate generated proteins with independent computational and experimental review.
anti_patterns: Do not treat generated proteins as ready for laboratory use.
Do not run large Forge batches without rate-limit and checkpoint handling.
Do not store sensitive sequences or tokens in shared cache files.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps with ESM3 generation, ESM C embeddings, structure workflows, inverse folding, and Forge API usage.

faq.question: Does it run models automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples that users can adapt in their own environment.

faq.question: Can I use it without Forge?
faq.answer: Yes. Some smaller ESM models can run locally, depending on hardware and package availability.

faq.question: What should I protect when using Forge?
faq.answer: Protect API tokens, private protein sequences, experimental data, and any regulated research material.

faq.question: Are generated proteins validated?
faq.answer: No. Model output requires independent structure, function, safety, and experimental validation.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
